root_cause: Pulse 2 (VA-EB-PL2) quality defect in lots PL2-2510/2511/2512
evidence: Replacement rate 31.9 per 100 orders in these three lot-months vs 5.1 in comparison Pulse 2 lot-months; tickets per 100 orders 86 vs 46; concentrated in Charging & Battery, Audio Quality, Warranty & Repair; volume wave Dec 2025 to Mar 2026 tracks the sales of those lots
confidence: High (lot-level, clear step change, dose-response by lot; causal mechanism not observable in this data)
owner_action: Quality/Manufacturing: root-cause the three lots and contain field stock; Support: lot-level early-warning trigger

root_cause: Defect-cohort tickets scored much lower on CSAT and drag the blended score
evidence: CSAT 2.77 on defect-cohort tickets (n=718) vs 3.42 on all other tickets; cohort is 13.8% of responses, worth 0.089 CSAT points overall
key_metric: blended CSAT lift if cohort scored like the rest
confidence: High for size of effect; medium for attribution (some of the cohort's low CSAT is handler/queue driven, see #3)
owner_action: Proactive outreach to owners of lots 2510-2512; fast-track replacement without a second contact

root_cause: Defect tickets were routed disproportionately to four Chat Frontline agents and to Tier 2
evidence: Of 1701 defect-cohort tickets, 317 went to A3004-A3007 (4 of 44 agents) and 448 to Tier 2; CSAT on those tickets 2.26 (rota four) and 1.88 (Tier 2) vs 3.39 for other Tier 1; rota four replaced 59% of them vs 16% for other Tier 1 agents
key_metric: share of defect tickets on 4 agents
confidence: Medium: routing concentration is observed; whether the rota got harder cases cannot be tested (no severity field)
owner_action: Spread hardware triage across the chat pool; give the rota a defect playbook (script, replace-or-repair rule)

root_cause: Residual coaching gap on the same four agents after adjusting for queue mix
evidence: Mix-adjusted CSAT gap -0.38 to -0.28 (z -2.8 to -4.2); gap is also present on non-defect charging tickets (non-defect Charging & Battery CSAT 2.51 vs 3.37 for other frontline agents); their CSAT gap to other chat agents was 0.27 before Oct 2025, widening to 0.91 in Dec 2025 to Mar 2026
confidence: Medium: statistically clear, but unobserved case severity could explain part of it
owner_action: Targeted coaching + QA sampling for these four; re-measure after one quarter

root_cause: Low raw CSAT for Logistics and Returns Desk agents is queue mix, not performance
evidence: Their mix-adjusted gap is small (Logistics -0.09 to +0.10; Returns Desk -0.06 to +0.07), inside noise; Delivery & Shipping and Returns & Refunds tickets average 3.20 CSAT for all handlers vs 3.42 overall
key_metric: raw bottom-ten agents whose gap is explained by mix
owner_action: Do not send these six agents to training; fix delivery/returns process instead

root_cause: Email first-response SLA misses (12.2% vs 6.4 to 8.6% elsewhere)
evidence: Breach rate by weekday 10 to 13%, by time-of-day block 11 to 15%, by month 6 to 18% (small monthly n): no clear peak-time driver, so capacity/queue order is the working hypothesis; breached tickets score CSAT 2.78 vs 3.38; 1014 attended breaches trigger Rs 350 credits each
key_metric: SLA credit cost (attended breaches x Rs 350)
owner_action: Capacity review of Email Frontline; consider priority ordering by SLA age
